title: Statistics & Averages: Frequency Tables, Estimated Mean, Stem-and-Leaf Diagrams, Choosing Averages & Comparing Distributions
description: Organise data with frequency tables, estimate the mean from grouped data, draw stem-and-leaf diagrams, choose the most appropriate average and compare distributions.

notes.heading: Frequency Tables

illustration.alt: A frequency table and a stem-and-leaf diagram shown side by side.
illustration.caption: Frequency tables and stem-and-leaf diagrams are two useful ways to organise and display data.

notes.body:
📌 Definition
A frequency table shows how often each value or group of values occurs in a data set.

🔑 How it works
Use tally marks to count, then write the frequency for each value. The total frequency is the number of data items.

| Score | Tally    | Frequency |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| 3     | `||`     | 2         |
| 4     | `||||`   | 4         |
| 5     | `|||`    | 3         |
| 6     | `|`      | 1         |

Total frequency = $2 + 4 + 3 + 1 = 10$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The mode is the value with the highest frequency.
• Adding all frequencies gives the total number of items.
• Frequency tables can use individual values or grouped class intervals.

notes.heading: Estimated Mean from a Frequency Table
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The estimated mean is found when data are grouped into class intervals by using the midpoint of each interval.

🔑 How it works
1. Find the midpoint of each class interval.
2. Multiply each midpoint by its frequency to get $fx$.
3. Add the $fx$ values.
4. Divide by the total frequency.

$$\text{estimated mean} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$$

💡 Worked Example
Find the estimated mean of these scores.

| Score   | Frequency | Midpoint | $fx$  |
|---------|-----------|----------|-------|
| $0-10$  | 3         | 5        | 15    |
| $11-20$ | 7         | 15.5     | 108.5 |
| $21-30$ | 5         | 25.5     | 127.5 |

Total $f = 15$ and total $fx = 251$.

$$\text{estimated mean} = \frac{251}{15} \approx 16.7$$

✅ Check
The answer lies inside the $11-20$ interval, which has the most data, so it is reasonable.

notes.heading: Stem-and-Leaf Diagrams
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A stem-and-leaf diagram shows each data value split into a stem and a leaf.

🔑 How it works
For the data set $23$, $25$, $31$, $36$, $42$:

Stem $2$: leaves $3$, $5$ represents $23$, $25$.
Stem $3$: leaves $1$, $6$ represents $31$, $36$.
Stem $4$: leaf $2$ represents $42$.

A key is essential:

$$1 \mid 4 = 14$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always order the leaves from smallest to largest.
• Always include a key.
• The median is the middle value when leaves are read in order.
• The range is largest value minus smallest value.

notes.heading: Mean, Median and Mode
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An average is a single value that represents a set of data.

🔑 Key Concept
• Mean: add all values and divide by how many there are.

$$\text{mean} = \frac{\sum x}{n}$$

• Median: the middle value when data are in order. For an even number of values, take the mean of the two middle values.
• Mode: the value that occurs most often. A data set can have more than one mode or no mode.

💡 Worked Example
Data: $4$, $7$, $8$, $8$, $10$.

Mean: $(4 + 7 + 8 + 8 + 10) \div 5 = 37 \div 5 = 7.4$.
Median: $8$ (the middle value).
Mode: $8$ (appears twice).

notes.heading: Choosing the Best Average
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The best average depends on the data and what you want to show.

🔑 How it works
• Use the mean when the data are fairly symmetrical and there are no extreme values.
• Use the median when there are outliers, because it is not affected by very large or very small values.
• Use the mode for non-numerical data or to find the most popular category.

💡 Worked Example
House prices in a street: $200000$, $220000$, $230000$, $240000$, $1800000$.

The mean is $(200000 + 220000 + 230000 + 240000 + 1800000) \div 5 = 540000$.
The median is $230000$.

The median is a better average here because the one very expensive house raises the mean too high.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Always using the mean without checking for outliers. Outliers can make the mean misleading.

notes.heading: Comparing Distributions
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To compare two distributions, look at their averages and their spread.

🔑 How it works
Compare:
• an average (mean or median) to see which group is typically higher or lower;
• the range to see how spread out the data are;
• the shape shown by a stem-and-leaf diagram or frequency table.

💡 Worked Example
Group A test scores: range $12$, median $72$.
Group B test scores: range $24$, median $68$.

Group A has a higher median, so Group A typically scores better. Group A also has a smaller range, so Group A's scores are more consistent.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Write comparisons in context.
• A larger range means the data are more spread out.
• A smaller range means the data are more consistent.

notes.heading: Range
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The range is a simple measure of spread.

🔑 Key Concept

$$\text{range} = \text{largest value} - \text{smallest value}$$

💡 Worked Example
For the data $14$, $19$, $21$, $23$, $27$:

$$\text{range} = 27 - 14 = 13$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to subtract the smallest value. The range is a single number, not the two values themselves.

questions.stem: What is the mean of $4$, $7$, $8$, $10$ and $11$?
questions.explanation: Add the values: $4 + 7 + 8 + 10 + 11 = 40$, then divide by $5$ to get $8$.
There are five values in order, so the median is the third value, $18$.
The value $5$ appears three times, which is more often than any other value.

questions.stem: The scores $2$, $3$, $3$, $5$, $7$ have a range of:
For the stem-and-leaf key $2 \mid 3 = 23$, what does $2 \mid 7$ represent?
questions.explanation: The stem $2$ means twenty, and the leaf $7$ means seven, so the value is $27$.

questions.stem: Find the midpoint of the class interval $20-30$.
A grouped frequency table has midpoints $5$, $15$, $25$ with frequencies $4$, $6$, $5$. What is $\sum fx$?
The total frequency in a table is $40$ and $\sum fx = 1200$. What is the estimated mean?
Which average is most affected by an outlier?
questions.explanation: The mean uses every value, so a very large or small outlier changes it. The median and mode are less affected.

questions.stem: Which average should you use to find the most common shoe size?
questions.explanation: The mode shows the value that occurs most often, which is the most common size.

questions.stem: In a stem-and-leaf diagram, how should the leaves be arranged?
choices: In order from smallest to largest
In the order the data were collected
questions.explanation: Leaves must be ordered from smallest to largest so the median and shape are easy to see.

questions.stem: Group X has median $65$ and range $15$. Group Y has median $72$ and range $30$. Which statement is true?
choices: Group Y is more spread out
Group X has a smaller median
questions.explanation: Group Y has a larger range, so its scores are more spread out. Group Y also has the higher median.

questions.stem: For the data $8$, $12$, $14$, $15$, $16$, $20$, what is the median?
questions.explanation: With six ordered values the median is the mean of the third and fourth values: $(14 + 15) \div 2 = 14.5$.

questions.stem: Which value is the outlier in $45$, $48$, $50$, $52$, $95$?
questions.explanation: $95$ is much larger than the other values, so it is the outlier.
